details.title: Working of Constitution
items: Establishes India as a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic
Ensures separation of powers among Legislature, Executive, and Judiciary
Provides Fundamental Rights to citizens for protection of liberties
Imposes Fundamental Duties to promote responsible citizenship
Implements Directive Principles for social and economic justice
Defines Union-State relations through federal structure
Regulates parliamentary democracy with elected representatives
Empowers independent institutions like Election Commission and CAG
Provides emergency provisions for national security and stability
Ensures judicial review to protect constitutional supremacy
Guarantees equality before law and equal protection
Supports local governance through Panchayati Raj and Municipalities
Maintains balance between rigidity and flexibility
Promotes social reform through constitutional provisions

details.title: Reviews
items: Judicial review by Supreme Court and High Courts
Interpretation of Constitution through landmark judgments
Review of legislative actions for constitutionality
Power to strike down unconstitutional laws
Public Interest Litigation for social justice
Review petitions for correcting judicial errors

details.title: Amendments & Reforms
items: Article 368 provides the procedure for constitutional amendment
Amendments can be initiated only in Parliament
Constitution Amendment Bills cannot be introduced in State Legislatures
Judicial review applies to constitutional amendments
Basic Structure Doctrine limits Parliament’s amending power
First Amendment (1951): Added reasonable restrictions to Fundamental Rights
First Amendment (1951): Inserted Ninth Schedule for land reforms
Seventh Amendment (1956): Reorganized states on linguistic basis
Ninth Amendment (1960): Adjusted territory after Indo-Pak agreement
Tenth Amendment (1961): Incorporation of Dadra and Nagar Haveli
Twelfth Amendment (1962): Incorporation of Goa, Daman and Diu
Thirteenth Amendment (1962): Special status to Nagaland
Fourteenth Amendment (1962): Puducherry made Union Territory
Twenty-Fourth Amendment (1971): Restored Parliament’s power to amend Fundamental Rights
Twenty-Fifth Amendment (1971): Limited right to property compensation
Twenty-Seventh Amendment (1971): Special provision for Mizoram
Thirty-Fourth Amendment (1974): Extended Ninth Schedule protections
Thirty-Sixth Amendment (1975): Sikkim became a state
Thirty-Ninth Amendment (1975): Protected election of PM and Speaker
Forty-Second Amendment (1976): Added Socialist, Secular, Integrity in Preamble
Forty-Second Amendment (1976): Strengthened Central Government powers
Forty-Fourth Amendment (1978): Restored civil liberties after Emergency
Forty-Fourth Amendment (1978): Made Right to Property a legal right
Fifty-Fifth Amendment (1986): Statehood for Arunachal Pradesh
Sixty-First Amendment (1989): Reduced voting age from 21 to 18
Sixty-Ninth Amendment (1991): Special status to Delhi (NCT)
Seventy-First Amendment (1992): Added Manipuri, Konkani, Nepali to languages
Seventy-Third Amendment (1992): Constitutional status to Panchayati Raj
Seventy-Fourth Amendment (1992): Constitutional status to Municipalities
Seventy-Seventh Amendment (1995): Reservation in promotion for SC/ST
Eighty-First Amendment (2000): Carry forward of vacancies
Eighty-Fifth Amendment (2001): Consequential seniority for SC/ST
Eighty-Seventh Amendment (2003): Delimitation based on 2001 Census
Ninety-First Amendment (2003): Limited size of Council of Ministers
Ninety-Second Amendment (2003): Added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, Santhali
Ninety-Ninth Amendment (2014): NJAC for judicial appointments
One Hundred and First Amendment (2016): Introduced GST
One Hundred and Second Amendment (2018): NCBC constitutional status
One Hundred and Third Amendment (2019): EWS reservation (10%)
One Hundred and Fourth Amendment (2020): Extended SC/ST reservation in legislatures
One Hundred and Fifth Amendment (2021): Restored State power over OBC lists
One Hundred and Sixth Amendment (2023): Women’s Reservation (33%)
Abolition of Right to Property as Fundamental Right
Strengthening of federal structure through reorganization acts
Reforms in electoral system through amendments
Social justice expansion through reservation policies
Protection of tribal and regional interests
Balancing parliamentary sovereignty and judicial supremacy
